html:
Roman emperor from 284 to 305, who ended the Crisis of the Third Century. Born Diocles to a humble family in Dalmatia, he rose as a cavalry officer and was proclaimed by the army in 284.

He decided the empire was too big for one man. He made Maximian co-emperor for the west, and in 293 added two junior emperors, creating the Tetrarchy. Other reforms:

  • He split the provinces into smaller ones and grouped them in dioceses, with civil and military jobs kept apart.
  • He made the army larger and set up a regular tax on land and people, based on a census.
  • He reformed the coinage and in 301 issued the Edict on Maximum Prices.
  • In 303 he began the Great Persecution of Christians.

In 305 he did something no emperor had done: he retired. He lived out his life in his great palace at Split, the Palace of Diocletian, and is said to have refused a call back to power, saying he preferred growing cabbages. He died around 311 as the system he built broke down and Constantine rose.
sum: Roman emperor from 284 to 305, who ended the Crisis of the Third Century. Born Diocles to a humble family in Dalmatia, he rose as a cavalry officer and was proclaimed by the army in 284.
